At Uma's request, Shiva explained the duties of householders, different castes, all castes, forest dwellers, sages, and the four stages of life, as well as reasons for changes in social status.
Uma asks questions about reincarnation, virtues leading to heaven, good and evil deeds, and conditions for knowledge and health.

Bhishma describes the different behaviors and fates of those who follow dharma and those who reject it, distinguishing between good and evil people.
Yudhishthira expresses confusion about why people sometimes fail despite effort, do good without prosperity, or study without happiness.
Bhishma explains to Yudhishthira that past karma and inherent nature determine future outcomes.

Bhishma teaches Yudhishthira that one must continuously perform actions while believing good deeds yield good results, with time as the ultimate driving force ensuring dharma does not lead to adharma.
Yudhishthira asks how to avoid sin and faults; Bhishma advises reciting lineages of gods and sages at dawn and dusk, listing numerous divine and sacred entities.
After Bhishma finishes teaching, Vyasa tells him that Yudhishthira and his brothers have attained inner peace and can return to their capital.
Bhishma blesses the Pandavas and instructs Yudhishthira to return to Kurukshetra when the sun turns northward, which will be his time of death.
Yudhishthira returns to Hastinapura with Krishna, Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, his brothers, and others.
Yudhishthira returns to Kurukshetra as instructed during Bhishma's final moments.
Bhishma comforts Dhritarashtra, saying inevitable events cannot be avoided, and urges him to treat the Pandavas as his own sons.
Bhishma turns to Krishna, requesting him to always guide and protect the Pandavas.
Bhishma asks the Lord of the World for permission to depart from life.
Bhishma dies, and his funeral is held; Yudhishthira and others go to the Ganges riverbank.
Ganga emerges from the turbulent waters, grieving for her son Bhishma, noting even Parashurama could not defeat him, but he died at Shikhandi's hands.
Krishna comforts Ganga, explaining Bhishma was a Vasu deity who temporarily lived on earth and has now returned to heaven as a Vasu.
Ganga calms down; after the funeral, everyone returns home.
